props.text: The client funds the escrow and reviews the contractor’s work. The account that sends the successful creation transaction becomes the client; the address below is the account being viewed.

Required: choose a reference such as invoice-2026-01. It must be unique for this client in this escrow contract, even after closure. Lookup uses the exact text, including case and spaces. The contract derives a separate agreement ID from the client address and reference.

The contractor accepts and submits work. The arbitrator can award disputed funds to either party. Both addresses are required: 0x followed by 40 hexadecimal characters. Replace the all-zero placeholders. Client, contractor and arbitrator must differ; neither entered address may be this escrow contract.
The arbitrator has no on-chain acceptance step. Naming an arbitrator does not confirm they have agreed to arbitrate.

The client sets this recipient when creating the agreement. This choice cannot be changed later. If the arbitration deadline passes with the dispute unresolved, anyone can call “Finalize arbitration timeout” to credit the full escrow to the chosen recipient. The recipient must withdraw it separately.

Enter a positive amount using either the native-asset or wei input. Native asset is this chain’s currency: 1 native asset = 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 wei. Creation locks this amount; transaction fees are separate.
All four durations are required whole seconds, from 1 to the maximum shown below. Phases start at the successful transaction’s block time; deadlines do not execute automatically.
Starts at creation. Before the deadline, the contractor can accept or the client can cancel. At or after it, anyone can finalize full credit to the client if acceptance is still pending.
Starts at acceptance. The contractor must submit before the deadline. At or after it, anyone can finalize full credit to the client if work is still unsubmitted.
Starts at submission. The client can approve or dispute before the deadline. At or after it, anyone can finalize full credit to the contractor if review is still pending.
Starts at dispute. The arbitrator can award the full escrow before the deadline. At or after it, anyone can finalize full credit to the chosen timeout recipient if the dispute is still unresolved.

Publish the agreed terms where the parties can retrieve them and enter that location in Terms URI (at most 512 UTF-8 bytes). Calculate the SHA-256 digest from a local file or a browser-readable URL, or enter it manually. Hash the exact document bytes. Local files are not uploaded or checked against the URI. Replace the all-zero placeholder before preparing creation; both fields are required.
Contract limits
Reference and URI limits count UTF-8 bytes; some characters use more than one byte.

funded means awaiting acceptance; accepted, awaiting work; submitted, awaiting client review; disputed, awaiting arbitration. cancelled and refunded states credit the client; released states credit the contractor. Closure records settlement, not withdrawal.

props.text: none means the viewed address is not a named party, or no account is selected. Any account can finalize an expired deadline; sending that transaction requires a wallet account.

The client funds and reviews; the contractor accepts and submits work; the arbitrator can award disputed funds. Naming the arbitrator does not confirm their consent: there is no on-chain acceptance step.
The amount funded at creation, also shown after settlement. 1 native asset = 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 wei.

Seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC. 0 means closed, with no timeout to finalize. For an active phase, ordinary phase actions stop at or after this deadline; finalizing its timeout still needs a transaction.
The client’s exact lookup reference; use it with the client address to find this agreement.

These durations were fixed at creation. Each phase starts at its successful transaction’s block time. The current phase is acceptance when funded, work when accepted, review when submitted, or arbitration when disputed.

Starts at dispute. The arbitrator can award the full escrow before the deadline. At or after it, anyone can finalize full credit to the chosen timeout recipient if the dispute is still unresolved.
The client chose this recipient at creation; it cannot change. An unresolved arbitration timeout credits them the full escrow when anyone finalizes it. Withdrawal is separate.

Terms are recorded by the client at creation, submission evidence by the contractor, and dispute evidence by the client. An empty evidence URI and all-zero digest mean it has not been recorded. A URI locates a document; the digest is the party’s claimed SHA-256 fingerprint of its exact bytes. Retrieve the file independently and compare its SHA-256 to check for matching bytes. This view and the contract do not fetch or verify documents.
